je_field.title: What the superconductor can carry
je_field.subtitle: Engineering current density of REBCO tape at 4.2 K. Measured to 31 T; everything beyond is the model's extrapolation.
je_field.note: A parametric fit representative of commercial 4 mm tape, not a datasheet.

hoop_ratio.title: A thicker coil does not escape the load
hoop_ratio.subtitle: Peak hoop stress in the winding, as a multiple of the magnetic pressure it produces.
hoop_ratio.note: Long coil, turns carrying their own load. The reference press is 7 % above this curve because it is short.

modulus_gap.title: The winding has to be stiffer than anything that exists
modulus_gap.subtitle: Stiffness of a winding that is half reinforcement, against what the superconductor's 0.4 % strain limit demands.

rows.label: T1100G carbon fibre
rows.detail: Reinforcement modulus 324 GPa at half the winding volume

rows.label: M60J carbon fibre
rows.detail: Reinforcement modulus 588 GPa at half the winding volume

rows.label: Record nanotube fibre
rows.detail: Reinforcement modulus 629 GPa at half the winding volume

rows.label: Nanosheet target (hypothetical)
rows.detail: Reinforcement modulus 300 GPa at half the winding volume

rows.label: Perfect graphene (ceiling)
rows.detail: Reinforcement modulus 1000 GPa at half the winding volume

modulus_gap.note: Reference press, safety factor 1.5. Colour marks how real the reinforcement is.

quench_margin.title: Every pulse quenches the superconductor
quench_margin.subtitle: Heat left in the tape by one field pulse, against the heat it can absorb before it stops superconducting.

y.label: Heat per pulse (MJ per m³ of tape, log scale)

rules.label: all the heat the tape can absorb (63 T design)

quench_margin.note: Margin 0.17 MJ/m³: 4.2 K to the current-sharing temperature at 63 T. Slower pulses lose less to eddy currents, but the hysteresis floor stays far above the margin.

power_rise.title: The faster the pulse, the larger the power station
power_rise.subtitle: Peak electrical power needed to raise the field in a given time: πE/2t.

energy_bore.title: Energy grows with the cube of the bore
energy_bore.subtitle: Field energy of a coil scaled from the reference press (build twice the bore, length five times).

discharge.title: One shot of the 10 ms press
discharge.subtitle: Current in the 37-turn coil. The bank is shorted at the peak so the current decays instead of ringing back.
discharge.note: 328 mF at 24.9 kV into 125 µH and 294 µΩ.

tube_radius.title: A copper tube under a magnetic pulse
tube_radius.subtitle: Radius of a 50 mm tube with a 2 mm wall during a pulse matched to the wall. Three of the four close the bore.
tube_radius.note: Rigid-plastic thin-shell model with field diffusion through the wall; no die or mandrel.

skin_heating.title: The surface pays for the pressure in heat
skin_heating.subtitle: Temperature rise of the eddy-current skin. Each dot is where that metal's surface reaches its melting point.

marks.tip: Mild steel skin melts at 117 T

skin_heating.note: A lower estimate (it ignores the resistivity rise of the hot skin). The interior stays near room temperature.

surface_pressure.title: Pressure along a billet is level in the middle only
surface_pressure.subtitle: Surface pressure on a 40 mm billet in the reference press, as a multiple of the nominal B²/2μ₀. The coil ends at ±250 mm.
surface_pressure.note: Perfect-conductor limit (the field stays out of the metal). The corner peaks, 2 to 6 times nominal, are off the top of the plot.

flow_stress_temperature.title: Pressure needed to keep a refractory metal flowing
flow_stress_temperature.subtitle: Required pressure at a strain of 0.3 and forming rates, against the temperature of the billet.
flow_stress_temperature.note: Constraint factor 1.2. Tungsten fits are calibrated to 1,000 °C; the rhenium curve is an estimate from tensile data.

grain_strain.title: One forming pulse does not make a fine grain
grain_strain.subtitle: Grain thickness against accumulated strain. Ultra-fine structures come from strains of three and more.
grain_strain.note: Geometric thinning towards the saturation size of severe plastic deformation; an estimate, not a fitted law.

weld_window.title: A weld needs a speed inside a window, at an angle
weld_window.subtitle: Aluminium 6061, 1 mm, onto steel. Too slow and nothing bonds; too fast and the interface melts or the collision outruns sound.
weld_window.note: Empirical limits from explosive welding (Deribas, Wittman, Cowan); drive across a 2 mm gap.

weld_drive.title: The pressures that weld sit well below the note's window
weld_drive.subtitle: Drive pressure that lands a 1 mm flyer inside its weld window across a 2 mm gap.

phase_diagram.title: Where diamond and cubic boron nitride are made
phase_diagram.subtitle: Equilibrium lines (two published models each) and the working points of industrial routes. Above a line, the hard phase is stable.

bands.label: concept note: pressure only, no heat, no dwell

phase_diagram.note: Nano-polycrystalline diamond (15 GPa and up) and carbon nitrides (72 GPa and up) are off the top of the scale.

route_dwell.title: Synthesis takes time that a pulse does not have
route_dwell.subtitle: How long each route holds its pressure and temperature. Only the two shock routes fit inside a magnetic pulse.

rows: resistive heating, Co infiltration from a WC-Co substrate

flyer_shock.title: The one route a pulse can run: throw a plate at it
flyer_shock.subtitle: Shock pressure in the sample when a 2 mm copper plate, driven over 10 mm, strikes it.
flyer_shock.note: Planar impedance match on linear Hugoniots; the graphite Hugoniots are estimates.

pore_collapse.title: Small pores are the hardest to crush
pore_collapse.subtitle: Pressure at which an isolated pore in titanium aluminide starts to collapse, against how much porosity there is.
pore_collapse.note: Hollow-sphere collapse, (2/3) σ ln(1/f), with no strain hardening: a lower bound on the pressure.

bond_time.title: Closing a pore is quick; healing it needs heat
bond_time.subtitle: Time for diffusion to bond the faces of a closed pore in titanium aluminide, against temperature.

rules.label: a magnetic pulse lasts this long

bond_time.note: Volume diffusion across 0.1 µm with an estimated prefactor; good to an order of magnitude at best.

powder_density.title: What a pressure pulse does densify: powder
powder_density.subtitle: Density of a loose metal powder after one pressure pulse, as a share of the solid.
powder_density.note: Plastic yielding of particles at pulse-rate strength, from random packing at 64 %. The step near 90 % is where the model changes from touching particles to isolated pores; the two laws do not quite join. The compact is not bonded and still needs sintering.

wall_ratio.title: How thick a steel wall must be
wall_ratio.subtitle: Outer radius over bore radius for a wall that contains the pressure with a 1.5 safety factor.

rules.label: practical limit of a one-piece wall

wall_ratio.note: A one-piece wall has no solution once the pressure passes its strength divided by 1.73: the curve ends there.

launcher_length.title: A launcher is as long as its payload is weak
launcher_length.subtitle: Length of a mass driver for a one-metre aluminium payload. The payload's strength sets the push, not the bore's.

series.name: if the payload could take 4 GPa

launcher_length.note: Base pressure capped at 184 MPa (aluminium 6061 yield over 1.5). No atmosphere, no sabot.
